feed.title: NPR Topics: Politics
feed.subtitle: NPR's expanded coverage of U.S. and world politics, the latest news from Congress and the White House and elections.

entry.title: Fetterman, already at odds with his party, makes surprise video for GOP convention
entry.summary: The Pennsylvania Democrat has already had a strained relationship with many inside his party. In the video, he spoke about working with Trump but did not outright praise him.

entry.title: Republicans kick off unconventional midterm convention in Dallas with Trump speech
entry.summary: Republicans' first midterm convention, being touted as a "Trumpapalooza" by the Republican Party chairman, kicks off in Dallas with a program focused heavily on tax cuts and border security.

entry.title: Andrew Tate is denied bail and will remain in jail during his extradition fight
entry.summary: Prosecutors told the court that Andrew and Tristan Tate boasted about having multiple passports and flying on private jets. But the Tates' lawyers argued they were only playing a role for their fans.

entry.title: Trump officials propose sweeping changes to the census that would reshape voting maps
entry.summary: A Trump census proposal would stop asking about race and exclude millions of U.S. residents from a count that the 14th Amendment says must include the "whole number of persons in each state."

entry.title: National Guard member arrested after drawing gun on fellow soldier in D.C.
entry.summary: A member of the Georgia National Guard deployed in Washington, D.C., as part of a task force to fight crime, has been arrested for pulling a gun on a fellow Guard member in an alleged dispute over regulation haircuts.

entry.title: Mail-in voters weigh flying to vote in person and other backup plans amid uncertainty
entry.summary: Voters and election officials are navigating uncertainty about mail-in voting for the midterms as the legal fight drags on over the U.S. Postal Service plan for President Trump's bid for restrictions.

entry.title: Ballot seizures seemed impossible. But judges and officials are prepping for them now
entry.summary: The idea of law enforcement taking possession of ballots in the middle of an active election used to be considered impossible. Now, it's a scenario voting officials — and judges — are training for.

entry.title: Trump promises $5,000 dividend in convention speech, but only if Republicans win
entry.summary: Calling it a "Trump dividend," the president announced a $5,000 payment for every adult citizen if the Republican Party maintains control of the House and Senate in the midterm election.

entry.title: The 2026 midterm general election season is upon us. Here's what to watch
entry.summary: The week of Labor Day marks the unofficial kickoff of the general election season. President Trump's unpopularity and Democratic enthusiasm means control of Congress is on the ballot.

entry.title: Republicans hope unconventional convention will rally voters ahead of midterms
entry.summary: The Republican party is calling it a "Trumpapalooza." The party is throwing an unconventional convention in Dallas this week to try to boost Republican voter enthusiasm.
